Kuvitus: pimeä luokkahuone. Pöydällä vas: Illustration: a dark classroom. On the table on the left there is a laser pointer on a small stand, and in front of it a thin transparent film mounted in a slide frame. The laser beam passes through the film, and faint rays fan out from the film to a white board on the right. On the board there is a horizontal row of evenly spaced red dots of light; the middle one is the brightest, and the dots become dimmer towards the edges.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: kaksi pa: Schematic diagram, not to scale: two panels one above the other. In both, plane wavefronts arrive from the left and hit a wall with a slit. In the upper panel the slit is many wavelengths wide: behind the slit the wavefronts continue almost straight, curving a little only at the edges, and the light travels as a narrow beam. In the lower panel the slit is as wide as the wavelength: behind the slit the wavefronts are semicircles, and the light spreads over a wide region, also behind the wall.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: Youngin: Schematic diagram, not to scale: Young's double-slit experiment seen from above. Plane wavefronts arrive from the left at a wall with two narrow slits S1 and S2. Circular wavefronts spread from each slit and overlap. On the screen on the right bright and dark fringes alternate; in the middle there is a bright fringe. Point P, which is the first bright fringe above the central fringe, is one wavelength farther from slit S2 than from slit S1.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: valon intensiteet: Graph to scale: the intensity of light on the screen relative to the largest value as a function of the path difference of neighbouring slits, with the path difference expressed in wavelengths from zero to 3.2. The dashed curve of the double slit varies smoothly: peaks at 0, 1, 2 and 3 and zeros halfway between them. The curve of the eight-slit grating has narrow, tall peaks at the same places, and between them the intensity is almost zero. The effect of the width of the slits is left out.
Kaavakuva, kulmat ja varjostimen etäisyy: Diagram with angles and screen distances to scale for a grating with 300 lines per millimetre. At the top, the situation seen from above: white light arrives from the left at the grating. The white central maximum, k = 0, continues straight through. On both sides of it the first-order light is spread into colours: violet, 400 nm, is deviated least, by 6.9 degrees, and red, 700 nm, most, by 12.1 degrees. At the bottom, the screen seen from the front at a distance of one metre from the grating: a white spot in the middle and on each side the first- and second-order spectra, with violet at the inner edge and red at the outer edge. The third-order spectrum already begins inside the second-order spectrum, so they partly overlap.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: hilan kaksi: Diagram, not to scale: two adjacent slits of a grating magnified. The distance between the slits is the grating spacing d. Light arrives from the left perpendicular to the grating. A parallel ray leaves each slit at angle theta to the original direction, which is shown by a horizontal dashed line. A perpendicular segment drawn from the lower slit to the ray of the upper slit separates off the extra distance of the lower ray, the path difference delta s. In the right-angled triangle whose hypotenuse is d and whose angle is theta, the path difference is d times sine theta.
Kaavakuva mittakaavassa ylhäältä nähtynä: Diagram to scale seen from above: on the left a laser whose beam hits the grating perpendicularly. The grating has 600 lines per millimetre, and the wavelength of the laser is 532 nm. One metre from the grating there is a screen. The light that goes straight through hits the screen at k = 0, and the first-order rays k = 1 and k = −1 are deviated by an angle of 18.6 degrees and hit the screen 33.7 cm on either side of the central maximum. The angle theta 1 is marked at the grating, the distance L from the grating to the screen and the distance x1 from the central maximum to the first maximum.
Kuvitus: pöydällä on CD-levy, jota valai: Illustration: a CD lies on a table, lit by a desk lamp from the upper left. On the silvery surface of the disc there are rainbow-coloured zones stretching from the centre to the edge, in which the colours are in order from violet to red.
Kaavakuva mittakaavassa ylhäältä nähtynä: Diagram to scale seen from above: on the left a laser whose beam hits the grating perpendicularly. The screen is 1.20 metres from the grating, and a scale in centimetres is drawn on its edge from zero at the central maximum, with numbers every twenty centimetres and short marks every ten centimetres. There are five light spots on the screen: the central maximum k = 0 at zero and k = 1 and k = 2 on both sides. The second-order spots are on the scale at 70 and minus 70 centimetres; the first-order spots are closer to the central maximum. The distance L from the grating to the screen is marked.
Kaavakuva mittakaavassa: varjostin edest: Diagram to scale: the screen seen from the front at a distance of one metre from the grating. White light passes through the grating. In the middle is the white central maximum, and on both sides of it there is a first-order spectrum with violet on the inner edge and red on the outer edge. Below the screen is a centimetre scale from zero at the central maximum, with numbers every five centimetres and short marks every centimetre, to 25 centimetres on the left and on the right. The inner edge of the spectrum is at about ten and the outer edge at about 18 centimetres. The line density of the grating is not marked.
